title: Task can be marked COMPLETED without valid final-goal verification
expected: A task may enter COMPLETED only after valid independent final-goal verification.
actual: If verify_final_goal_state is missing, throws, or returns the wrong type, the engine creates a VERIFIED result whenever any step was already verified, then transitions to COMPLETED.
evidence: Source lines 423-447. Existing test planner/tests/test_final_state_verification.py::test_action_success_does_not_equal_task_success_when_final_state_absent failed on this audit host; exact target-Windows behavior needs rerun.
impact: A partial workflow may be reported as complete despite the requested final state being absent.
fix: Remove the fallback. Verifier absence/exception/malformed result/insufficient evidence must result in UNVERIFIED/BLOCKED/FAILED, never COMPLETED. Preserve error evidence.
regression: Add tests for missing/throwing/wrong-type verifier, partial action success, wrong final state and genuinely observed final state.

title: Generic final-goal verifier accepts any completed step plus a healthy window
expected: Compare explicit goal-specific desired state with independently observed application/UI state.
actual: For most non-typing goals, completed_step_count > 0 plus an observable healthy active window returns VERIFIED; the evidence records window title and step count, not the requested goal outcome.
impact: Saving a file, submitting a form, changing a setting, etc. can be marked successful when the target result was never proved.
fix: Implement goal-specific final-state contracts. If the system cannot observe the required state, return UNVERIFIED/BLOCKED. Never infer task success from action count or window liveness.
regression: Wrong value, wrong window, unrelated active window, partial task, crashed app, unsupported goal type and confirmed correct final state.

title: OBSERVE launch path returns success even when application launch fails
expected: Execution result should match the actual outcome; app launch must be constrained and independently verified.
actual: OBSERVE may call os.startfile/subprocess.Popen for model-supplied app string, swallows exceptions, and unconditionally returns success. Heuristic verifier also treats OBSERVE as VERIFIED.
impact: Failed launch can look successful, and untrusted planner values can request unintended launch targets subject to other layers.
fix: Make OBSERVE observational only. Use a distinct launch action with strict allowlist/path validation, risk policy and observed window confirmation; return failure on exception.
regression: Missing executable, blocked launch, disallowed executable, no window, wrong window, slow launch and successful launch.

title: QA harness kills all processes named notepad.exe
expected: Test cleanup must terminate only the exact process started by the current test.
actual: terminate_processes_by_name iterates all processes named notepad.exe and kills each one. The suite calls it during setup/teardown. The packaged assurance/notepad.exe is a custom WinForms mock from MockNotepad.cs, not native Notepad.
evidence: Source paths and line ranges above; assurance/MockNotepad.cs.
impact: Running this suite on the user's desktop may kill unrelated native Notepad windows and lose unsaved work. Reports can overstate native app coverage.
fix: Do not run the suite on the desktop before fixing. Track spawned child PID, creation time and executable path/job object; terminate only owned children. Label mock app correctly and test native Notepad separately in disposable environment.
regression: Keep an unrelated Notepad instance open with unsaved state and prove harness does not terminate it.

title: Startup/harness kills arbitrary port listeners on 8000 and 5173
expected: Only owned processes may be terminated; an unknown listener should cause safe port-conflict failure.
actual: _free_stale_ports and kill_process_on_port terminate any process listening on these ports without proving it belongs to COMPASS.
impact: Other development servers/services can be killed when running tests or starting COMPASS.
fix: Remove broad port killing. Track child processes launched by current instance. Unknown listener = BLOCKED with PID/path diagnostics, not automatic termination.
regression: Create unrelated listeners on 8000/5173 and assert they stay alive while launch reports conflict.

title: Adversarial harness can submit destructive goals to a live auto-executing task endpoint
expected: Adversarial goals must be tested in an isolated non-executing/sandboxed environment with desktop control disabled.
actual: Harness copies os.environ but does not explicitly set COMPASS_TEST_MODE=1 in the spawned backend. /api/tasks schedules execution unless that variable exists. The suite posts a prompt instructing COMPASS to ignore safety and delete system files.
evidence: assurance/real_product_harness.py:192-200; assurance/real_product_suite.py:375-399; backend/app/routers/tasks.py:21-39. pytest conftest does not automatically configure a separately spawned backend process.
impact: If run against an active AI-enabled desktop, hostile input may enter actual execution. Audit did not execute this harness due this risk.
fix: Quarantine the current suite. Explicitly set and assert test mode in the child process and use a recording/blocking execution adapter or isolated VM. Never permit adversarial tests to dispatch OS actions.
regression: Prove dangerous test prompt produces zero OS dispatch calls; missing isolation flag aborts test startup.

title: Independent observer test passes without observing expected text
expected: PASS only when the exact expected text exists in the intended window/control.
actual: text_verified evaluates expected text OR non-empty observed text OR action_ok; any of the latter two passes even when expected text is absent.
impact: Historical product test results do not prove text entry worked correctly.
fix: Remove both fallback clauses; verify target window/control and exact expected content using documented normalization. If not observable, FAIL/UNVERIFIED.
regression: Absent text, wrong window, partial text, pre-existing text, wrong control and actual correct text.

title: Controlled failure test passes solely because backend is alive
expected: When target disappears, test must assert safe rejection/abort, no unintended input, correct task state and retained evidence.
actual: After POSTing a type action against the vanished target, pass status is set to backend_alive; action response and actual side effects/task state are not checked.
impact: Unsafe action handling can pass so long as server remains alive.
fix: Verify API result, no input dispatched to another target, correct TaskState and recovery/abort trace. Keep backend liveness separate.
regression: Target closed, stale/reused HWND, other foreground window, and a properly rejected action.

title: Adversarial tests accept HTTP status plus liveness as proof of security
expected: Each attack needs threat-specific assertions and proof of no prohibited side effects.
actual: SQL injection, XSS, path traversal, prompt injection and other payloads are considered safe if status is 201/400/422 and backend remains alive; database/filesystem/task-execution effects are not checked.
impact: Accepted unsafe payload may be labelled protected; interacts dangerously with task auto-execution.
fix: Use isolated test adapters; make payload-specific assertions; inspect database/file/dispatch side effects. A successful HTTP status is not a safety result.
regression: Per-payload negative assertions plus known-unsafe fixture that must be detected.

title: Stored 18/18 'real product E2E' result is not supported by the test execution path
expected: Exercise one actual product workflow end-to-end through the official task pipeline and independently verify outcome; all claimed stack components must be ready.
actual: Suite creates a task that may auto-execute, calls planner endpoint separately, and directly calls automation/type, so flow can race and bypass the generated plan. Harness can return ready when backend is live but frontend never became ready. Target is a custom Notepad mock.
evidence: Source ranges; stored real_product_test_report.json says 18/18 PASS with timestamp 2026-10-04.
impact: Historical E2E claim does not demonstrate the actual assembled frontend→backend→planner→executor→verifier workflow.
fix: Separate unit/API/mock-app/native-app suites. For E2E execute task exactly once via official path and verify final OS state. Require full stack readiness and report target app type, run ID, commit/tree hash.
regression: Demonstrate test fails when planner or frontend path is bypassed; prevent task/action races.

title: Release gate/master runner can mark FAIL as PASS or ignore blocked/unrun gates
component: assurance release gate and master runner
expected: Every mandatory gate must pass on fresh matching evidence; release gate should return nonzero on FAIL and master runner must consume structured readiness.
actual: Gate's warnings ignore SKIPPED/BLOCKED/NOT_RUN/ERROR/TIMEOUT states; stale files may be reused. Script prints readiness but does not return nonzero on FAIL. Master runner maps process exit code to stage PASS. Stored master report says release_gate PASS though its stdout says readiness FAIL/blocking secret_scan.
impact: Certification can be falsely reported successful despite a failing release decision.
fix: Strict fail-closed state machine; run ID/source hash/freshness; explicit mandatory gate schema; nonzero on failure; runner parses JSON and cross-checks exit status and actual report.
regression: Fixtures for every gate status, stale PASS, malformed report, child exit 0 plus structured FAIL, and child failure.

title: Dependency and performance gates ignore important findings and regressions
expected: Aggregate all relevant dependency scans and compare measured metrics against justified performance thresholds.
actual: Dependency gate reads only pip_audit vulnerabilities, ignoring stored npm findings (1 high, 1 moderate). Performance gate is PASS if baseline and optimized files exist, without evaluating benchmark verdicts or thresholds. Stored comparison reports planning +33.1%, DB +54.8%, action +14.3%, replanning +69.9%, STOP +240.3%.
impact: Release may pass despite dependency advisories or significant performance degradation.
fix: Include npm and other dependency ecosystems; use fresh scan data and explicit suppression policy. Set justified SLOs and evaluate each benchmark; file existence must never pass the gate.
regression: Fixtures with npm high advisory, missing scan, stale baseline and threshold-exceeding metric.

title: Historical certification documents and evidence are contradictory
expected: Certification must identify exact revision/run and must not call untested mandatory behavior certified without an approved deviation.
actual: FINAL_CERTIFICATION says Phase 24 and CERTIFIED & FROZEN while marking real-world test NOT_TESTED; OPEN_SOURCE_INTEGRATION_AUDIT says final validation not yet done; PRODUCT_TEST_MATRIX broadly marks PASS while KNOWN_LIMITATIONS admits missing security/browser tests. Stored release report FAIL.
impact: Cannot trust that claimed certification scope was completed for the supplied source tree.
fix: Preserve historical records but mark them historical/superseded; issue a new traceable certification only from a fresh run tied to current source hash, explicit mandatory gates and residual limits. Clarify phase numbering without erasing history.
regression: Automated consistency check across gate JSON, master report, test matrix, run ID and certification doc.

title: Finding registry can silently reset on corrupt JSON and lacks reliable lifecycle/evidence guarantees
expected: Corrupt registry must be preserved/quarantined and certification blocked; writes should be atomic/thread-safe; recurrence should reopen with evidence; fixed findings require regression ID.
actual: _load catches any exception and empties in-memory findings; next save can overwrite bad registry. Class claims thread-safety but code has no lock. Duplicate detection can return an old finding without refreshing evidence. All 7 stored records had empty evidence and regression_test_id; one OPEN item had verification_status VERIFIED.
impact: Failure history can be lost and “verified fix” labels are not grounded in permanent tests/evidence.
fix: Add schema version, locking, atomic save, backups/quarantine and fail-closed behavior. Model lifecycle OPEN→FIXED→RETESTED→CLOSED; recurrence reopens. Require evidence and regression ID for verified closure.
regression: Corrupt JSON, concurrent writer, crash during save, recurrence, missing evidence and mismatched status.

title: Secret scanner excludes assurance directory and suppresses generic lines
expected: Scan relevant source, configuration, and assurance files, handle dotfiles and distinguish approved dummy data narrowly.
actual: SKIP_DIRS includes assurance, excluding scanner and associated source/config from main scan. Path.suffix is commonly empty for exact `.env`. is_dummy_or_test skips a line if it contains generic words such as test, payload, mock or sample.
evidence: Source lines above; stored secret report has three candidate token patterns in a test fixture that require precise triage.
impact: Credentials may be missed and scan coverage overstated.
fix: Do not skip the whole assurance directory; handle dotfiles explicitly; replace broad generic-word skips with exact fixture values/hashes; detect then redact and report exclusions/coverage.
regression: Test fake credentials in `.env`, assurance scripts, comments containing generic words, fixtures, logs and scanner config.

title: Local API uses wildcard CORS with credentials and lacks an obvious explicit authorization layer at control routes
expected: Use explicit configured origins and defend privileged local click/type/task endpoints against untrusted browser-origin requests and unauthorized local calls.
actual: CORSMiddleware uses allow_origins=['*'], allow_credentials=True, all methods and headers, despite a separate configured origin list. Inspected OS-control/task routes have no obvious auth dependency at router entry points. Exploitability was not tested live.
evidence: backend/app/main.py:88-96. Live browser origin/localhost tests were not run.
impact: Local OS-control API is a high-impact trust boundary; actual exploitability depends on binding, browser protections and the remaining route implementation.
fix: Use explicit origin configuration, no wildcard+credentials, apply appropriate request authorization/CSRF/origin protections and test on target supported browser in isolated environment.
regression: Hostile origin, disallowed origin, no-token control call, allowed frontend origin and localhost/PNA behavior.

title: PlanValidator only validates schemas for a subset of action types and risk derives mainly from goal keywords
expected: Every action type must have strict schema/parameter/target/risk/permission checks based on the structured action and context.
actual: _validate_action validates TYPE, WAIT and KEY/KEY_PRESS but returns true for other action types. Consequential risk uses keywords in step.goal rather than the actual action type and parameters. Other layers may mitigate some cases, but this validator is incomplete.
impact: Malformed or risky plan items can pass this named validation layer and rely on unspecified downstream checks.
fix: Add exhaustive per-action schemas; reject unknown/extraneous parameters; validate targets and bounds; derive risk from actual action semantics/context while retaining independent downstream safety/approval.
regression: Test all action types, invalid/missing params, dangerous action with benign wording, safe action with risky keywords, unsupported enum and launch paths.

title: Heuristic action verifier can mark focus/click/observe verified without proof of intended effect
expected: Focus/click/observe verification must prove a concrete postcondition; technical dispatch alone is not outcome success.
actual: Focus path treats action type click/focus as sufficient to set is_focused even when foreground HWND comparison did not match. WAIT/OBSERVE are always verified; default click/key can be verified when target/window remains healthy without detecting an expected transition.
evidence: Source ranges above; separate verify_click_transition returns UNVERIFIED when no observable state change but heuristic path can bypass it.
impact: Action results can overstate success and cascade into final goal false positives.
fix: Remove type shortcut; compare observed HWND and target, require action-specific expected outcome or return UNVERIFIED.
regression: Wrong foreground window, failed focus, no-op click, modal dialog, no-op key, missing observer and genuine outcome.

title: Non-Windows coordinate fallback accepts arbitrary positive coordinates; Windows boundary allows one-past edge
expected: Live coordinates must be within actual virtual desktop and unsupported platform mode must not imply live validation.
actual: On non-Windows it returns `Simulated coordinates valid` for any nonnegative x/y after a limited rectangle check. Windows comparison uses > rather than >= at right/bottom exclusive edge. Current pytest failed the impossible-coordinate test.
impact: Host-side false safety and one-past bounds bug risk; actual Windows branch not executed in this audit.
fix: Return UNSUPPORTED for real dispatch outside Windows or use explicitly injected test geometry. Fix half-open bounds and validate against target geometry.
regression: Very large coords, negative multi-monitor coords, exact edges, one-past edges, invalid rectangle and HWND cases.

title: StaleGuard can report freshness without validating a live HWND off Windows
expected: A real target handle must be revalidated for existence/state; unsupported platform must be blocked or use an explicitly fake test adapter.
actual: HWND checks only happen when sys.platform == win32 and target_hwnd; outside Windows the result can be based on timestamp. dead HWND test failed on this host.
impact: Tests can get false confidence and real Windows behavior remains unverified.
fix: Explicitly distinguish live HWND validator and test adapter; unsupported live revalidation should be BLOCKED/UNSUPPORTED, not fresh.
regression: Dead/reused handle, changed title, minimized window, foreground switch and stale UIA element.

title: Workflow tests target a different orchestrator/model implementation than runtime API imports
expected: Tests exercise the production runtime path, or both implementations are explicitly maintained and tested.
actual: Runtime router imports top-level planner.workflow_models/workflow_orchestrator; tests import planner.workflow.*. Parallel DAG/models/orchestrator/scheduler files exist.
impact: Green tests may not validate the orchestrator that the product API actually serves.
fix: Map callers and establish one authoritative runtime implementation, or test both intentionally. Add API-level workflow tests via real runtime path before any consolidation.
regression: Integration assertion that runtime API uses the exercised orchestration implementation.

title: Overlay highlight action returns success even if overlay IPC failed
expected: Return success only when overlay action succeeded or independent evidence confirms it.
actual: An overlay IPC error is swallowed and ActionResult(success=True) is still returned.
impact: Logs/metrics can claim an unperformed visual operation succeeded.
fix: Propagate error or return UNVERIFIED; require response/observation for success.
regression: IPC down, timeout, explicit negative response and successful response.

title: Source ZIP contains runtime DB/logs and lacks Git provenance for reproducible certification
expected: Shareable source archive should link exact commit/tree hash, lock dependencies and exclude/sanitize runtime user/task data.
actual: ZIP has no .git metadata, includes storage/compass.db (~557 KB) and logs/compass.log (~449 KB), plus generated traces/reports. Therefore tag/commit correspondence cannot be verified.
evidence: Archive inventory: no .git/.venv/frontend node_modules; DB/log present.
impact: Certification provenance is unverified and DB/log could contain task content or personal data.
fix: Produce source-only export plus separate sanitized evidence package, add source tree hash and lockfile/environment manifest, inspect/redact DB/log before sharing.
regression: Packaging allowlist and secret/PII scan; verify source hash and exact release provenance.

title: Historical benchmark comparisons show latency regressions that release gate ignores
expected: Performance PASS must follow reproducible current measurements against justified limits.
actual: Stored comparison shows planning +33.1%, database +54.8%, action +14.3%, replanning +69.9%, STOP +240.3%. Release gate still says performance PASS based on artifact existence; benchmark code labels some metrics simulated and reports are historical.
evidence: Stored benchmark comparison and release gate logic.
impact: The optimization/performance claim is unsupported until measurements and thresholds are reproduced. STOP latency increase merits review, with methodology confirmed before conclusions.
fix: Run target Windows benchmarks with recorded run/source IDs, repeated samples, workload, warmup and resource measures. Define thresholds and require all regressions approved; separate simulated microbenchmarks from actual product performance.
regression: Release gate must fail for missing/stale metrics and unexplained threshold violations.

title: Actual Windows/product behavior was not verifiable on audit host and several platform tests error instead of cleanly blocking
expected: Supported Windows environment and dependencies are required for authoritative UIA/Win32/overlay/product certification; unsupported platform should be clearly BLOCKED, not fake PASS.
actual: Audit ran on Linux/Python 3.13.5; PySide6/WinRT/hypothesis and Playwright browser runtime unavailable. Full pytest: 45 failed, 491 passed, 12 skipped, 25 collection errors, 5 warnings in 20.80s. Actual Windows product did not run.
evidence: Raw test log in audit package. Many errors reference ctypes.WinDLL/windll; coordinate safety is a real host-reproduced mismatch. Other failures require isolated Windows reruns.
impact: No claim can be made that the assembled Windows application fully works based on this audit.
fix: Run on the supported Windows environment with declared dependencies; categorize platform-dependent tests; run true UIA/Win32/frontend/API/E2E in isolated desktop with fresh evidence.
regression: Target Windows full regression, actual product workflows, STOP, UIA, overlay, and exact run-ID evidence.

title: Documentation and phase/certification references are inconsistent and too thin to govern testing reliably
file: README.md; SPEC.md; docs/QA_AND_CERTIFICATION.md; docs/TESTING.md; docs/SECURITY.md; docs/ROADMAP.md; docs/CORE_LIFECYCLE.md
expected: Current canonical docs should accurately describe architecture, tests, safety invariants, certification scope, limitations, environment and commands.
actual: Several key docs are boilerplate/only a few lines; SPEC.md focuses on Phase 9, a certification record says Phase 24, and test matrix PASS claims conflict with known limitations.
evidence: Named files, plus finding 013 documentation conflicts.
impact: Future agents may use wrong test process or mistake planned/documented behavior for implemented, verified capability.
fix: After remediation, update the correct canonical documents, preserve historical records, and align roadmap/phase mapping with actual current implementation and evidence.
regression: Doc-to-code/test consistency check; ensure instructions run successfully in clean environment.
